thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: HIGH-LATENCY on /v1/generate (region: us-west-2) — triggered by error-rate spike > 5% and p95 > 1200ms. Pages: @Maria Chen (oncall), @Suresh Patel (eng-sre) — please ack and triage.

Maria Chen: acked. jumping in. seeing a burst of long tails around 16:42 UTC. looks like continuous batching backlog grew. investigating queue lengths.

Suresh Patel: looking now — attaching recent `nginx` tail:```
nginx: upstream_response_time: 1.23, 0.98, 3.12, 10.45
worker queue depth: 42, 47, 63
cpu 90% on pod inference-3
```

Maria Chen: thanks. check routing policy — are we spilling to cheaper tier? could be a routing fallback loop.

Jordan Lee: quick note — the runtime reported several KV cache evict events just before the latency spike. logs show load of a new model variant and a rollback attempt. suspect cache thrash + compaction.

Anya Koval: heads-up — support flagged two paying customers saw 503s. not wide but visible. need impact classification before postmortem ask.

Ben Torres: can we get a quick damage assessment? severity depends on customer impact + duration.

Maria Chen: current scope: ~3 minutes full p95 spike, intermittent errors for ~10m window. 2 paying customers (Acct-A, Acct-B) reported degraded throughput. I'd call this sev2 (customer-impacting but partial). thoughts?

Suresh Patel: agree sev2. root of instability appears to be a new autoscaling policy + aggressive fallback to low-cost variant which triggers cold KV loads. Fix: adjust fallback policy + add short-term pad to autoscale.

Olivia Park: for mitigation, rolling a config change sounds safest. I can push a conservative change to routing policy and set autoscale min replicas + disable cheap-variant fallback for 30m. need approval to proceed.

Maria Chen: go for it. do the change, monitor p95 and error-rate. note the canary flag so we can revert quickly.

incident-bot: ACTION: Mitigation deployed by Olivia Park at 16:58 UTC — routing fallback disabled, autoscale min=3. Observed p95 drop to 220ms within 90s.

Jordan Lee: confirmed. KV eviction events stop after stabilizing. collecting follow-up tasks now.

Anya Koval: schedule post-incident review? prefer sooner rather than later while context fresh. propose 60m async write-up + 1h postmortem meeting tomorrow.

Ben Torres: +1. Also need explicit action items: owner, size, priority, and whether it ties to Q3 roadmap (we're doing performance work).

Maria Chen: I'll draft the incident summary in #postmortems and tag owners. rough list from me:
- AI1: investigate autoscale/fallback interplay and root cause of policy loop — owner: Jordan Lee — size: medium (3-5d) — priority: P0 (must fix for stability) — tie: Q3 reliability epic.
- AI2: add KV cache health metrics and alerting (evict-rate > X) — owner: Suresh Patel — size: small (2d) — priority: P1 — tie: Q3 observability backlog.
- AI3: customer outreach + RCA for Acct-A/B — owner: Anya Koval & Ben Torres — size: small (1-2d) — priority: P0 (customer SLA) — tie: Q3 support improvements.
- AI4: canary policy formalization + staged fallback runbook — owner: Olivia Park — size: medium (4d) — priority: P1 — tie: Q3 rollout controls.

Suresh Patel: adding one:
- AI5: emergency short-term config guard (prevent fallback if cache eviction > threshold) — owner: Suresh Patel — size: tiny (half day) — priority: P0 (mitigate recurrence).

Jordan Lee: can take AI1. estimate 4d because need perf tests across seq lengths + kernel checks. will open tasks and link perf harness.

Anya Koval: I'll own AI3. planning customer notes and timeline. will coordinate with CS and legal if needed.

Ben Torres: proposal for prioritization matrix: severity x customer-impact x sprint capacity. For Q3 tie-in let's tag AI1 and AI2 as roadmap-critical, AI4 as planned improvement, AI3 as immediate customer SLAs.

Maria Chen: agree. let's size in story points for tracking: tiny=1, small=3, medium=8. update items accordingly.

Olivia Park: scheduling note: put AI1/AI2 on next sprint triage and flag for engineering-planning sync. AI5 I can ship today as emergency patch.

Suresh Patel: will open the alert ticket and add sample query for evict-rate metric.

incident-bot: NOTE: postmortem draft requested by Maria Chen. Postmortem meeting suggested: 2025-08-22 15:00 UTC (tomorrow) — organizer: Ben Torres.

Ben Torres: creating calendar invite now, adding doc link. please add any logs/links to doc pre-meeting.

Maria Chen: closing loop: final ask to oncall rotation — if any repeat of spike, escalate immediately to paging level 2 and avoid manual fallback toggles without owner sign-off.

Jordan Lee: copied. will push CI perf regression tests to catch KV-thrash pattern.

Anya Koval: will draft customer communication and postmortem action table.

Olivia Park: will ship AI5 guard and post config change as PR.

Suresh Patel: will follow up with alert thresholds and SLA-derived runbook steps.

Maria Chen: thanks team. marking thread for post-incident follow-up and linking to quarterly planning board (Q3 reliability). :white_check_mark:
